detailed_description:
Photoreal cinematic live-action, 1881 London, 35 mm film grain, natural weight and pace.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:04. The shot begins from <Picture 2>: an insert across the sofa seat: the violin stands with its chinrest under a pale jaw at the TOP of frame, its body the length of a forearm, the scroll of its neck at the LEFT, the bow laid across the strings at the CENTRE a hand's span longer than the violin; <Subject 1>'s thin pale left hand is closed round that neck, the shirt cuff turned back at the wrist, amber gaslight along the varnish; only what <Picture 2> shows is in frame. The camera is on the red Turkey carpet at the room's centre, a hand above the seat, three feet from the violin. At the first frame The violin stands with its chinrest under Holmes's jaw at the TOP of frame and its scroll out at the LEFT, the four strings and the bridge across its belly. The camera tilts up a hand's breadth toward the sofa back as the left fingers drop a finger's width down the violin's neck toward the nut, from 00:00 to 00:04.
[Shot 2] From 00:04 to 00:08. At 00:04 the shot cuts to a medium close shot on <Subject 1> half raised against the rolled sofa arm, bare-headed, dark hair swept back, beginning from <Picture 3>: the violin under his chin, his left hand round the neck, the bow on the strings in his right hand with the white plaster on the forefinger, the eyes shut, the bottle-green velvet shoulder in the lower LEFT, the drawn heavy red curtain behind his head, amber gaslight on his cheek from off the LEFT edge. The camera is on the red Turkey carpet at the room's centre, a little below his shoulder, five feet from the head of the sofa. At the first frame Holmes sits half up with his back against the rolled arm at the RIGHT. The camera pushes in a foot toward his shut eyes and the sofa back as the bow draws two inches along the strings, from 00:04 to 00:08. <Subject 1>'s mouth is closed from 00:04 to 00:05 while he bow draws two inches along the strings.
